presentation.guidance: Prose is the natural carrier for causal semantics; code anchors are optional and must not dominate.

allowed.carrier: narrative prose (causal logic structure)
allowed.when: Single causal problem narrative; not ≥2 column-aligned comparable items.

forbidden: Before→after comparison tables or success-state tables
Structure diagrams or flowcharts

required: State the problem and its cost at the user-perception or system-behavior level
The problem statement is logically independent of GOAL/SCOPE/IF content—does not preview conclusions
forbidden: Opening with file paths, module names, or code structure (belongs in SCOPE/ST)
Steps, commands, or phase markers

presentation.guidance: Comparative semantics naturally suit contrast carriers; structural outcomes must cover engineering-visible dimensions (e.g. module coupling, deployment independence), not only user-visible behavior.

allowed.carrier: Before→after comparison table (before → after, one row per dimension)
allowed.when: ≥2 observable dimensions sharing before|after columns.

forbidden: Narrative prose goal statements (without before/after contrast)
Scope tables or architecture diagrams

required: Goal statements must be observable: one can judge whether they are met, not merely a direction
Before→after contrast view covering behavior-visible or structure-visible dimensions
forbidden: Restating the CTX problem narrative (avoid duplication)

presentation.guidance: Show in-scope surfaces and explicit out-of-scope/deferred items in one boundary view. Each exclusion should bind to the goal or invariant it protects; trade-off rationale belongs in DECISION, not SCOPE.

allowed.carrier: Scope mapping table (touch surface → nature of change)
allowed.when: ≥2 in-scope surfaces sharing surface|change columns.

allowed.carrier: Exclusion item list (excluded path | protected boundary/invariant)
allowed.when: ≥2 exclusions sharing excluded|protected columns.

required: When more than two scope items, present in structured form (object → nature of change)
In-scope and out-of-scope (or deferred) both present when exclusions exist
forbidden: Repeating SCOPE's in-scope list

presentation.guidance: When multiple paths were genuinely considered, a comparison structure is the natural carrier for reasoning semantics; row count is determined by the number of paths actually considered. When only a single direction was considered, do not force a contrast table.

allowed.carrier: Direction comparison table (direction | conclusion | design rationale | reopen conditions)
allowed.when: ≥2 genuinely considered directions sharing direction|conclusion|rationale|reopen columns.

allowed.carrier: Narrative reasoning (single decision, no genuine contrast paths)
allowed.when: Single considered direction; no genuine contrast set.

forbidden: Phase, Owner, or Timing tables

required: Design reasoning for the chosen direction (grounds beyond stakeholder authorization)
When multiple considered paths exist, provide a comparable contrast view
forbidden: Chosen-direction rationale that is only a stakeholder-authorization citation (belongs in SCOPE/GOAL)

presentation.guidance: Invariants are a set of independent propositions; each stands on its own—even if other entries are obscured, each can still be judged true or false in isolation. Nested dependencies or pure reference-chain forms break this independence and do not meet this standard.

allowed.carrier: Numbered independent constraint list (each stands alone)
allowed.when: ≥1 independent invariant; each entry truth-evaluable alone.

forbidden: Phase tables or step lists

required: When invariants are present, each is semantically self-standing (truth value can be judged without depending on other entries)
forbidden: Entries that only say "see IF" / "see GOAL" / "see SCOPE" with no invariant content

presentation.guidance: When choosing a carrier, use as the criterion whether a reviewer can read the relation semantics directly from the carrier without inference; the carrier is determined by the content's relation type. When content includes dependency relations, directed forms (A → B) convey direction semantics—a responsibility-assignment table does not convey direction and does not meet this standard. When content includes state transitions, a structured view of state / trigger conditions / terminal state conveys state-machine semantics—narrative sentences do not meet this standard.

allowed.carrier: UML diagram (Mermaid classDiagram / sequenceDiagram / stateDiagram)
allowed.when: Relation type needs class/sequence/state semantics readable without inference.

allowed.carrier: C4 architecture diagram (Mermaid C4Context / C4Container / C4Component)
allowed.when: Context/container/component topology is the relation type.

allowed.carrier: Directed flowchart (Mermaid flowchart / graph)
allowed.when: Directed dependency or control flow (A → B) is the relation type.

forbidden: Tables of any kind (directed-dependency tables, responsibility tables, and data-flow tables all fail)
Narrative sentences describing state transitions

required: When the design introduces new modules, components, or services: annotate name and responsibility boundary
All names must be identifiable system artifacts—existing ones, or explicitly marked as new
forbidden: Opening with architectural positioning or design rationale (belongs in DECISION)
Option comparison and rationale for rejected alternatives (belongs in DECISION)
Task steps, file-change inventories, or Run commands (belongs in tech-plan)
Decorative diagrams that do not convey structural semantics
Placeholder names such as "some module" or "related service"

presentation.guidance: Use a table only for ≥2 isomorphic items under shared columns; otherwise use a bullet list.

allowed.carrier: Comparable contract table
allowed.when: ≥2 items share the same column meanings (fields, named slots, or multi-path end-states).

allowed.carrier: Caller-facing contract norms
allowed.when: Normative claims that are not comparable under one shared column schema.

forbidden: Single-row or mixed-axis tables (one claim only, or rows that do not share column meanings)
One undifferentiated IF surface mixing address, named faces, and exercise outcomes when more than one caller question is in scope

required: When more than one field or endpoint: present cross-boundary semantics in structured form
When interaction or visible outcomes change: provide terminal-state semantics for success, warning, and failure paths
Data schemas, naming conventions, or feature-flag contracts: when defining more than one element, use a structured form suited to the contract type

Contract entries must include function names, command names, typed field definitions, or schema names—behavioral descriptions of data flow (e.g. "the query layer returns candidates") do not meet this requirement
forbidden: Standalone path-specific discourse that duplicates table-row content

presentation.guidance: Name both sides of each seam and assign obligations or forbidden cross-boundary demands. Prefer a two-sided obligation table over prose wishlists.

allowed.carrier: Two-sided obligation table (provider / consumer / must-not)
allowed.when: ≥2 seams sharing provider|consumer|must-not columns.

allowed.carrier: Bullet norms naming both sides
allowed.when: Seam norms not column-aligned under one shared schema.

allowed.carrier: Sequence sketch of handoff
allowed.when: Handoff order/sequence is the primary seam substance.

required: Both sides of each seam are named
Obligations or prohibitions are assigned
forbidden: Seam as aspirational wishlist without owner

presentation.guidance: Acceptance intent, verification method, and pass signal together constitute a complete evidence chain; items without a pass signal cannot be used for acceptance.

allowed.carrier: Acceptance matrix (acceptance intent | verification method | pass signal | design-error signal)
allowed.when: ≥2 acceptance items sharing intent|method|pass|error columns.

forbidden: Standalone test-strategy tables that heavily overlap acceptance-matrix rows

required: Each acceptance intent maps to a verification method and a decidable pass signal
At least one falsifiable condition (with a clear failure state)
When closing a verification gap, record closure in DECISION/settled facts; process blockers via stage agenda
forbidden: Restating the SCOPE exclusion list as regression-test prose

presentation.guidance: Expose known risks, fragile assumptions, accepted costs, and open questions. Prefer a risk/open-question table; do not rewrite locked norms as soft risk language.

allowed.carrier: Risk / open-question table
allowed.when: ≥2 risks/open questions sharing comparable risk columns.

allowed.carrier: Bullet norms for accepted costs
allowed.when: Accepted-cost norms; not a multi-row risk matrix.

required: Risks or open questions are explicit when bets exist
forbidden: Empty risk section when known bets remain

presentation.guidance: Technical dependencies are a continuous design narrative at responsibility grain: which external technical entities this design depends on, what version or capability changes are committed, whether peers must change in sync, and where this design sits in that chain. A short structured view is fine for listing independent dependencies without turning the section into a project schedule, RACI, structural diagram (ST), or contract field table (IF).

allowed.carrier: Prose stating external technical dependencies, upgrades, and placement
allowed.when: Dependency narrative without ≥2 column-aligned dependency rows.

allowed.carrier: Short dependency table (party | dependency or upgrade | readiness/sync condition | placement)
allowed.when: ≥2 dependencies sharing party|dependency|readiness|placement columns.

forbidden: Overall structural diagrams or interaction topology

required: State whether external technical dependencies (release collaboration and/or dependency upgrades) are in scope for this demand
When in scope: name external parties/dependencies, version or capability commitments when relevant, and placement or readiness/sync conditions at design level
forbidden: Project schedules, owners, or RACI matrices
Repeating IF contract field definitions
Traffic-shifting strategy detail that belongs to RISK when exposing uncertainty, or to ST/IF/I for concrete operability norms
Replacing ST structural narrative with only a dependency list
